cues.text: Excuse me, Dr Twain. May I speak with you for a minute?
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: Of course, please come in.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: I’m Charlotte York. I’m considering taking your course in Tourism.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: Right. Well, Charlotte, how can I help you?
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: Would you mind answering some of my questions?
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: Absolutely, fire away!
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: Well I have been discussing courses with my parents and they are concerned that I will not be able to get a well-paid job with a degree in Tourism.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: The reason that I want to study the course is that I have a great interest in the subject and I think I would really enjoy it.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: I believe the only way that I will enjoy my life is if I enjoy my career.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: Happiness is far more important than money, don’t you think?
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: Absolutely. I would much rather be happy and poor rather than rich   and miserable. Money cannot buy you happiness.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: I’m glad you agree.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: You needn’t worry about money, Charlotte.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: A large part of the Tourism course is dedicated to teaching students how to manage ﬁnances, a skill that you can apply to your everyday life as well.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: I would also recommend that you take a sideline course in time management, as this can be incredibly useful in efficiently planning your workload. Efficiency is the key to success!
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: I’ll remember that.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: Now I have found that some students have natural talents that really help them to succeed in the course.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: Communication skills, for example, can be very beneficial. Do you have any strengths?
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: Maths was always my favourite subject at school so I really enjoy solving mathematical problems, however I ﬁnd statistics quite diﬃcult.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: I have always been very capable and selfsuﬃcient.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: I have a lot of conﬁdence in my abilities  and  will  take  the  initiative  in  situations  without  needing  to  depend  on anyone else for their help.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: That’s a really great quality to have and will be particularly useful if  you choose to study Tourism.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: That’s great.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: I would recommend that you spend some of your time researching the course.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: A lot of people who are uneducated on the subject claim that Tourism is a shrinking industry and that it will become irrelevant in the future.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: If you study the published research however, you will see that the truth is quite the opposite.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: The industry has, in fact, grown signiﬁcantly as people have developed an ever-increasing interest in culture and travel.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: Have you compared the university course with a polytechnic?
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: Yes, I have. I was interested in studying the course in modules.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: However, the university doesn’t oﬀer that option.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: Don’t have enough funds  to be able to attend an expensive university, so I was relieved to see that the course is quite aﬀordable.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: I also considered attending a summer school instead of university to save money and so that I could work during the rest of the year, but I really wanted the university experience.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: I think that university would suit you well.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: Now, what about the courses? Are you interested in any of the other subjects on offer?
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: I have looked at a few. I was interested in Travel and Business as it sounds similar to Tourism.
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: That is really worth learning, Q26 however, be aware that it is diﬃcult and will demand a lot of your time.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: OK, that’s good to know.
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: You might ﬁnd that an interesting course and it will teach Japanese is you valuable skills in speaking the language.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: Personally, it’s not bad and could be of some help, but not that much.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: OK, Japanese, got that.. .What about Medical Care?
cues.speaker: MELANIE

cues.text: Well, if you have time, the course will teach you a lot about curing diseases and illnesses, or dealing with injuries outside, although it’s not essential.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: So, OK,  if it’s useful, I’ll take it.
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: If you enjoy using technology and are worried about fulﬁlling the entry requirements, computing is very relaxed about the skills that applicants must possess.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: I’m terrible with computers so I’m not sure that I would enjoy that course. How about Public Relations?
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE

cues.text: Yes, I would recommend that course.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: It would be related to entering the Tourism industry as it will educate you on how to approach clients and develop associations with them.
cues.speaker: DR TWAIN

cues.text: That’s great! Thank you so much for your help!
cues.speaker: CHARLOTTE
